findings.title: Use of Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs breaks supported runtimes
findings.body: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were introduced in Python 3.13. On earlier supported Python versions, `q.shutdown(...)` raises `AttributeError` (which is only logged here), leaving workers blocked forever in `get()`. Each subsequent `worker.join(timeout=5.0)` then waits the full timeout, so the default 20 queues can make every consumer shutdown take roughly 100 seconds and leak daemon workers. An exception raised while processing work also attempts to resolve `queue.ShutDown` in the exception handler and can terminate the worker with an `AttributeError`. Use a compatible sentinel/event-based shutdown mechanism or require and enforce Python 3.13.

findings.title: Closing one assignment permanently disables the factory-owned pool
findings.body: The pool is created once on `ResultsStrategyFactory` and is shared by every strategy returned from `create_with_partitions`, but `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` shuts that shared pool down. After a Kafka partition revoke/reassignment causes Arroyo to close/terminate one strategy and create another from the same factory, the new strategy receives the already-shut-down pool and no workers. On Python 3.13, `Queue.put()` then raises `ShutDown`, and `submit()` catches that error and marks the offset complete, so the new strategy can commit messages that were never processed. On older Python versions, the puts succeed into queues with no workers and offsets never advance. The pool must be scoped to a single strategy assignment or recreated/reset after strategy teardown.

findings.title: The worker queues are unbounded, so the new mode provides no backpressure
findings.body: `queue.Queue()` defaults to `maxsize=0`, meaning `FixedQueuePool.submit()` never blocks regardless of how far a slow worker falls behind. The consumer will continue decoding and retaining every fetched message (including both the decoded result and original `Message`) in memory while lag grows. A slow remote-subscription handler can therefore cause unbounded memory growth and OOM the consumer, contrary to the strategy's stated backpressure guarantee. Configure a bounded queue size and integrate blocking/full-queue handling with the consumer's polling/backpressure behavior.

findings.title: The purported graceful shutdown abandons queued work before a final commit
findings.body: Workers are marked `shutdown=True` before their queues are shut down. A worker that is currently processing exits after that item, and a worker that was blocked in `get()` processes at most one item before its next loop-condition check exits; remaining queued items are never drained. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` also stops and joins the commit thread before this worker shutdown, so an item finishing during shutdown has no later commit opportunity. This causes arbitrary accepted work to be replayed after normal deploys/rebalances, potentially duplicating side effects and creating large restart backlogs. Shutdown should drain accepted work (or deliberately cancel it with a coordinated retry policy) and commit completed offsets after the drain.
